name: Slow-moving stock and markdown plan
summary: Before a seasonal reset, the merchandiser or store owner gets one plan from the sales and stock exports: each item's sell-through and weeks of cover, the cash tied up in dead and slow stock, and a markdown plan in dated steps with the margin each leaves and a date to stop. The owner decides every price.

sources.title: Fully Powered AI's own design: sales and stock exports with set column headers that stop on a mismatch; a keep-or-clear mark on every item; default markdown steps of 20, 35 and 50 per cent off the full price; a margin floor stated as a margin on the reduced price; a stop date a set number of days before the reset; a check figure of units sold since the first markdown that decides whether each later step is taken; the margin per unit, in per cent and if every unit sold, at each step; no forecast of extra sales from a lower price; kept lines above a cover limit raised as questions instead of marked down; and an approval line on each item's plan.

sources.contribution: Sell-through as units sold over units sold plus units on hand, stock measured in time left at the current pace, no recent sales as the sign of dead stock, a thirty-day grace period for new arrivals, an item with no recent sales labelled as such, with no cover figure worked out from a zero, cash at cost put ahead of unit counts, deeper cuts for stock that is selling less, bundling as an exit, and a review timed before a seasonal reset.

Marking down when stock will outlast the time left in the season, a deeper opening step when the expected sell-through is under 40 per cent, reductions that grow in stages and come closer together as the season end nears, a margin limit no price may break and a cap on the deepest cut, and outlets, clearance buyers or donation for what is left.
